segments.activity: Read geography, explain words and sketch sea/coast/inland
Read and select relevant community evidence

materials: Printed passages, paper and pencil. A pupil may describe a sketch orally or direct a scribe.
support: Read each record aloud without supplying the comparison. During guided work only, offer room/path headings. Independent responses must retain the same reasoning demand with oral or scribed access.
extension: Identify a new observation that would change the recommendation and explain why. Compare two different defensible recommendations that use the same evidence.
factualScope: The order is Regions of Liberia. Stable physical geography is used; no historical narrative, current population, official safety policy or officeholder claim is added. These would require separately verified sources.

sourceChecks.scope: Geography only. No historical dates, population estimates, current officeholders or official policy claims are used.

sources.title: Overview of Liberia, Ministry of Local Government
sources.locator: National Overview, geographical setting and landscape paragraphs
usedFacts: Liberia is in West Africa beside the Atlantic Ocean.
Its terrain includes coastal lowlands and interior hills, plateaus and mountains.
sources.reuse: Original short paraphrase only. No website map or photograph copied. Distribution-rights review remains pending.

sources.title: FAO, Liberia: Geography, population and water resources
sources.locator: Geography, population and water resources, first paragraph
usedFacts: The physical terrain includes coastal plains, hills, plateaus and mountainous areas.
sources.limits: Historical country profile. Its old demographic, economic and agricultural statistics are not used. Exact elevation cutoffs are not presented as universal boundaries.
sources.reuse: Original short paraphrase, not a quotation; independent academic and rights review pending.

sourceChecks.fictionalEvidence: All reading-club sites, paths, observations and community decisions in the lesson are explicitly invented teaching cases, not measurements from a real school.
sourceChecks.mapping: Physical regions are generalized terrain descriptions, not county borders. Learner sketches have no scale and cannot locate a real site precisely.

originalWording: No map, photograph or long text is copied. Geographic statements are short original paraphrases; fictional records are labelled on first presentation. Exact-version rights and academic review remain pending.
oversight: Read the full comparison and recommendation. Check use of both records, separation of observation/inference, a counterargument and an honest uncertainty. Formative choice success is not independent mastery evidence.
safety: No outdoor investigation is required. Adults must decide actual venue and route safety; pupil writing is a reasoning exercise, not authorization to use a site.
offline: Keep geography and both case records available in print. Use a paper sketch or oral description. Do not require an online map, color discrimination, dragging, a field trip or a real location disclosure.
retention: Propose a different pair of local records after seven days. Ask for a comparison and a limited conclusion. Nothing is scheduled or scored here.
assessment: All work is formative. No governed test, official grade, promotion decision or canonical mastery update is supplied.
